title: Zero mean under coordinate independence
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<p<1$, let $h:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and choose a coordinate $i$. Suppose replacing coordinate $i$ by any sign leaves $h$ unchanged. Under the product distribution of independent signs with probability $p$ of $-1$, the mean of $h(x)$ times the standardized sign in coordinate $i$ is zero; here the standardized sign is the sign centered at its mean and divided by its standard deviation.
hypotheses_covered: $h$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
